mission_08: Reproducibility is the cornerstone of scientific machine learning. Every experiment must be fully reproducible, meaning that running the same code with the same data produces identical results. This requires careful management of random seeds across all components (data splitting, model initialization, cross-validation folds), recording of all hyperparameters and configuration choices, and systematic logging of results. An experiment runner framework encapsulates this discipline by defining experiments as configurations, running them with controlled randomness, and recording complete metadata including scores, timing, and environment information. This approach enables fair comparison between different pipelines, tracking of experiment history, and confident reproduction of results. Reproducible experimentation is essential for research, regulatory compliance, and building trust in ML systems.
